questions.stem: What is the name for the change of state from solid to liquid?
questions.explanation: Melting is the change of state from solid to liquid. It occurs at the melting point of the substance.

questions.stem: During a change of state, what happens to the temperature of the substance?
questions.explanation: During a change of state, the temperature remains constant even though energy is being supplied or removed. The energy is used to break or form bonds between particles.

questions.stem: Which change of state involves a substance going directly from solid to gas?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through the liquid state. An example is dry ice (solid CO2) turning into gas.

questions.stem: During melting, energy is used to:

options.text: Increase the temperature of the substance
Break bonds between particles so they can move more freely

questions.explanation: During melting, the energy supplied breaks the bonds between particles, allowing them to move from fixed positions (solid) to moving freely around each other (liquid).

questions.stem: Which change of state releases energy to the surroundings?
questions.explanation: Freezing (liquid to solid) releases energy because bonds are being formed between particles. Melting, boiling, and evaporation all absorb energy.

questions.stem: How does evaporation differ from boiling?

options.text: Evaporation only occurs at the surface and at any temperature; boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a specific temperature
Boiling happens at any temperature; evaporation only at the boiling point

questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs only at the surface of a liquid and can happen at any temperature. Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a specific temperature (the boiling point).

questions.stem: The change of state from gas to liquid is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change of state from gas to liquid. It releases energy to the surroundings as bonds form between particles.
